neighbours.label: ' in' opening a fixed adverbial phrase inside a clause ('thanks in part', 'which in turn', 'that in places')
fire: The team won the title, thanks in large part to its defense.
Exercise raises dopamine, which in turn improves mood.
Sales grew last year, due in part to lower prices.
The roads, which in places were flooded, stayed closed.
The city's growth was driven in large measure by the port.
The policy failed, in part because nobody enforced it.
Rising prices reduce demand, and this in turn lowers output.
The project succeeded thanks in no small part to volunteers.
quiet: The team won the title in a close final last May.
Exercise raises dopamine in the brain within minutes.
Sales grew last year in most of the stores.
The roads in the valley were flooded and stayed closed.
The city's growth was driven by the port in the north.
The policy failed in the spring because nobody enforced it.
Rising prices reduce demand in the housing market.
The project succeeded with help from volunteers in town.
